grammarFocus: 转述动词；引述与改写；限定词 some / most / all 的范围。
title: Media, Information and Evidence: The Campus Podcast
instructions: 这是一份模拟练习材料，不是官方雅思考试。请先听录音（或阅读录音稿），然后完成10道题。题目类型包括单选、填空和正误判断（True/False/Not Given）。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有解释均为中文，证据为英文原文引用。
transcript:
Mia: Welcome back to Campus Voices. I'm Mia Chen, and today we're talking about how students check information online. With me is Daniel Wu, a second-year journalism student. Daniel, thanks for coming.
Daniel: Thanks for having me, Mia. So, the other day I was reading a news story about a new study on coffee and sleep. The headline said 'Coffee causes insomnia in all students.' I thought that was too strong.
Mia: Right. What did you do?
Daniel: Well, first I looked for the original study. The article said 'researchers claim' but didn't name the university. I found the study on a university website. It said 'some students who drank coffee after 6 p.m. had trouble sleeping.' Not all students. And it was only 50 people.
Mia: So the headline exaggerated the findings.
Daniel: Exactly. The journalist used the verb 'claim' which suggests doubt, but then the headline said 'causes' which is very strong. Also, they didn't mention the sample size.
Mia: What about social media? Do you think most students check facts before sharing?
Daniel: Honestly, I think most students don't check. I read a survey from our own university that said 70 percent of students share news without reading the full article. But that's just one survey. I wouldn't say 'all students' do that.
Mia: So you're careful with words like 'all' and 'most'.
Daniel: Yes. In journalism, we say 'some' means a few, 'most' means more than half but not all, and 'all' means every single one. If you use 'all' when you only have evidence for 'some', that's misleading.
Mia: Can you give an example of how to report speech accurately?
Daniel: Sure. If a scientist says 'I think there might be a link,' you shouldn't write 'Scientist says there is a link.' You should write 'The scientist suggested there might be a link.' The verb 'suggest' is softer than 'say' or 'claim'.
Mia: So the choice of reporting verb matters.
Daniel: A lot. 'Claim' can suggest the person is not reliable. 'State' is neutral. 'Admit' suggests they did something wrong. So we need to be careful.
Mia: What advice do you have for our listeners?
Daniel: Check the original source. Look at the numbers. Ask: does the evidence support the words 'all' or 'most'? And when you share, use careful language. Say 'some studies suggest' not 'studies prove'.
Mia: Great advice. Thanks, Daniel.
Daniel: Thank you, Mia.

questions.prompt: What was the headline of the news story Daniel read?
options: Coffee causes insomnia in all students.
Some students who drink coffee have trouble sleeping.
Coffee is bad for students' health.
answers: Coffee causes insomnia in all students.
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔明确提到标题是“Coffee causes insomnia in all students.”。其他选项要么是原文中的其他句子，要么是错误概括。
questions.evidence: The headline said 'Coffee causes insomnia in all students.'

questions.prompt: According to the original study, who had trouble sleeping?
options: Some students who drank coffee after 6 p.m.
Most students who drank coffee in the morning.
Students who did not drink coffee.
answers: Some students who drank coffee after 6 p.m.
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔引用研究原文说“some students who drank coffee after 6 p.m. had trouble sleeping.”，不是所有学生。
questions.evidence: It said 'some students who drank coffee after 6 p.m. had trouble sleeping.'

questions.prompt: How many people were in the study? (Write a number.)
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔说研究只有50人。答案来自原文“only 50 people”。

questions.prompt: What does Daniel say about the verb 'claim'?
options: It means the person is lying.

questions.evidence: The journalist used the verb 'claim' which suggests doubt

questions.prompt: What percentage of students share news without reading the full article, according to the survey?
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔提到调查说70%的学生分享新闻前不读全文。
questions.evidence: a survey from our own university that said 70 percent of students share news without reading the full article.

options: More than half but not all

questions.evidence: 'most' means more than half but not all

questions.evidence: You should write 'The scientist suggested there might be a link.' The verb 'suggest' is softer than 'say' or 'claim'.

questions.prompt: According to Daniel, what does the verb 'admit' suggest?
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔说“'Admit' suggests they did something wrong.”。

questions.explanation: 丹尼尔建议说“some studies suggest”而不是“studies prove”。

grammar.title: 转述动词与限定词的范围（some / most / all）
grammar.explanation: 在转述别人的话时，动词的选择会影响意思。例如，say 是中性，claim 可能暗示怀疑，suggest 更柔和，admit 暗示做错了事。另外，some 表示“一些”，most 表示“大多数（超过一半但不是全部）”，all 表示“全部”。使用时要根据证据选择准确的词，避免夸大。
grammar.example: The scientist suggested there might be a link.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reporting verb: The manager ______ that there might be a delay, but he wasn't sure.
questions.explanation: 因为经理不确定，用 suggested 更合适，表示“暗示/提出”。claimed 可能暗示怀疑，admitted 暗示做错事，stated 太肯定。
questions.evidence: The verb 'suggest' is softer than 'say' or 'claim'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'more than half but not all'?
questions.explanation: most 表示“大多数”，即超过一半但不是全部。
questions.evidence: 'most' means more than half but not all

questions.prompt: The report says '______ students passed the exam' but the data shows 100%. Which word is correct?
questions.explanation: 数据是100%，所以用 all 表示全部。

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence to report a scientist who is not sure:
options: The scientist proved that the drug works.
The scientist admitted that the drug works.
The scientist suggested that the drug might work.
The scientist claimed that the drug definitely works.
answers: The scientist suggested that the drug might work.
questions.explanation: suggested 和 might 表示不确定性，符合科学家不确定的情况。其他选项都太肯定或带有负面含义。
questions.evidence: The scientist suggested there might be a link.

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (about 120 words) for a school magazine advising students how to check information online. Use at least three reporting verbs (e.g., claim, suggest, admit) and the words some, most, all correctly.
